title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Discover the unique customs of Agnes Scott College, from century-old class rivalries and onyx ring ceremonies to the modern ritual of ringing the bell for career success.

cards.title: Black Cat Week
cards.subtitle: A Century of Class Rivalry
cards.notes: Participate in a week of spirit competitions ending in a bonfire. It began in 1915 as a prank night between first-years and sophomores.
cards.short_summary: Black Cat is a week-long spirit competition and orientation finale that has defined the Agnes Scott experience since 1915.
cards.evidence_claim: Black Cat began in 1915 as a prank night between first-year students and sophomores and now marks the end of orientation.
cards.access_notes: Held annually in the fall, typically concluding orientation for new students.

cards.title: Sophomore Ring Ceremony
cards.subtitle: The Iconic Black Onyx
cards.notes: Receive your class ring, a black onyx stone inscribed with 'ASC'. This rite of passage has united generations of Scotties since 1935.
cards.short_summary: A formal ceremony where sophomores receive their signature black onyx class rings, a tradition dating back to 1935.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sophomore Ring Ceremony is a rite of passage where students receive onyx rings inscribed with 'ASC' and their class year.
cards.source_title: Sophomore Ring Ceremony - Agnes Scott College
cards.access_notes: Occurs during the sophomore year; family and friends are invited to attend.

cards.title: Ringing the Bell
cards.subtitle: Celebrating Post-Grad Success
cards.notes: Head to the Main Hall tower to ring the bell after landing a job or grad school spot. Sign your name inside the tower for posterity.
cards.short_summary: Seniors ring the historic bell in Main Hall to announce their post-graduation plans, such as job offers or graduate school acceptances.
cards.evidence_claim: Since 1992, seniors ring the bell in Main Tower when they receive a job offer or graduate school acceptance.
cards.source_title: ASC Decoded: Ringing the Bell – Perspective
cards.access_notes: The bell is located in the tower of Main Hall; ringing typically occurs on Friday afternoons in the spring.

cards.title: Senior Investiture
cards.subtitle: The Parade of Leaders
cards.notes: Watch the senior class parade through campus in their academic regalia. This ceremony formally recognizes seniors as campus leaders.
cards.short_summary: An annual fall ceremony and parade that honors the senior class as they begin their final year at the college.
cards.evidence_claim: Senior Investiture began in 1908 and was reimagined in 2021 to include a campus-wide parade and community picnic.
cards.access_notes: Held at the start of the academic year on the Main Quad.

cards.title: Honor Code Signing
cards.subtitle: A Commitment to Integrity
cards.notes: Sign the Honor Pledge during orientation to join a community of trust. This tradition grants students freedoms like self-scheduled exams.
cards.short_summary: New students formally sign the Agnes Scott Honor Pledge, a cornerstone of campus life that dates back to 1906.
cards.evidence_claim: During orientation, each student pledges support to the Honor System and individually signs the Honor Code in Buttrick Hall.
cards.access_notes: The signing ceremony takes place in Buttrick Hall during new student orientation.

cards.title: Pancake Jam
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Finals Fuel
cards.notes: Eat pancakes served by faculty and staff to fuel your late-night study sessions. Enjoy music and dancing before the exam period begins.
cards.short_summary: A late-night breakfast event held every semester before finals where faculty and staff serve pancakes to students.
cards.evidence_claim: Pancake Jam is a twice-yearly event where faculty and staff serve breakfast food to students from 9pm to 10pm before exams.
cards.access_notes: Held in Evans Hall; pancakes are typically served from 9:00 PM to 10:00 PM.

cards.title: AgnesPalooza
cards.subtitle: Spring Semester Celebration
cards.notes: Celebrate the return from spring break with a week of festivals and dance parties. Each year features a unique theme and live events.
cards.short_summary: A week-long spring festival featuring music, dancing, and themed activities to celebrate the second half of the semester.
cards.evidence_claim: AgnesPalooza began in the 1990s and is a week full of events including a festival and dance party held after spring break.
cards.access_notes: An annual spring event; locations vary across campus based on the year's theme.

cards.title: Founder's Day
cards.subtitle: Honoring the College's Roots
cards.notes: Celebrate the college's 1889 founding every February. The event features speakers and performances reflecting on the school's mission.
cards.short_summary: An annual celebration in February that commemorates the founding of the college and its history.
cards.evidence_claim: Founder's Day dates back to 1918 and is celebrated every year, usually in February, with speakers and student performances.
cards.source_title: Agnes Scott Traditions | Campus Traditions & Student Life
cards.access_notes: Held annually in February; open to the entire campus community.

cards.title: Rushing the Quad
cards.subtitle: Midnight Spirit Kickoff
cards.notes: Join your classmates at midnight on the Monday of Black Cat week to decorate the Quad in your class color.
cards.short_summary: A midnight ritual where students decorate the central campus quad in their specific class colors to kick off Black Cat week.
cards.evidence_claim: Students begin Black Cat at midnight on Monday with 'Rushing the Quad' to decorate in their class color.
cards.access_notes: Occurs at midnight on the first Monday of Black Cat week on the Main Quad.

cards.title: Junior Jaunt
cards.subtitle: Legacy of Charity and Skits
cards.notes: Learn about this historic fundraiser where classes performed skits and crowned a queen based on money raised for charity.
cards.short_summary: A historic tradition from the 1950s-1980s involving class skits and fundraising for charity.
cards.evidence_claim: Junior Jaunt (1954-1980) was an event where the class that raised the most money for charity had a representative crowned Queen.
cards.access_notes: This is a defunct tradition, now preserved in the college's historical archives.
